skill.name: software-engineer
skill.description: Builds and refactors code safely; prefers small diffs, clear validation steps, and testable outcomes.
skill.summary: Guides careful software engineering work with small patches, repo-aware changes, and clear validation steps.
skill.author: ACSKamloops

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 11 tells the assistant to avoid destructive actions unless explicitly requested, which is a safety guardrail rather than reconnaissance or malware behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid destructive actions unless explicitly requested.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 11 instructs the assistant to avoid destructive actions unless explicitly requested. This is a safe operational guardrail, not system reconnaissance or malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Software changes can become hard to review when scope grows or validation is unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward small patches, repo-aware decisions, and concrete checks.
actual_capabilities: Prompts clarifying questions when requirements are ambiguous.
Prioritizes existing repository patterns and utilities.
Asks for validation steps when behavior changes.
Discourages destructive actions without explicit user approval.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not include scripts or automation.
Does not define language-specific coding standards.
Requires access to the target repository for best results.
Does not replace human review or project-specific tests.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Focused Module
use_cases.description: Improve a small part of a codebase while preserving current behavior and keeping the diff reviewable.

use_cases.title: Implement a Clear Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Turn a known defect into a scoped patch with an explicit validation command or test target.

use_cases.title: Review an Ambiguous Request
use_cases.description: Identify missing requirements before implementation so the final change matches the project need.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the software-engineer skill. Make the smallest practical change for this request, follow existing repo patterns, and include one validation step.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the software-engineer skill. Investigate this bug, ask clarifying questions if needed, implement a narrow fix, and report how to verify it.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Without Behavior Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Moderate refactor that needs careful scope control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the software-engineer skill. Refactor this area without changing behavior, prefer existing utilities, and keep the diff easy to review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and Validate a Risky Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced change with unclear blast radius.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the software-engineer skill. First assess ambiguity and risk, then propose a compact implementation plan and validation strategy before editing files.

output_examples.input: Add a validation check to a form handler.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the existing validation pattern, applies a small handler update, and suggests the focused form test to run.

output_examples.input: Refactor a service method that has duplicated branching.
output_examples.output: The assistant keeps behavior unchanged, extracts the repeated decision path, and recommends the existing service test suite for validation.

output_examples.input: Implement a vague performance improvement request.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for target metrics, affected workflows, and acceptable tradeoffs before proposing code changes.

best_practices: Give the assistant a specific file, feature, or failing behavior.
Share expected validation commands when the project already defines them.
Review proposed destructive or broad changes before approving them.
anti_patterns: Requesting a large rewrite without defining the target behavior.
Skipping tests or validation after behavior changes.
Adding new dependencies before checking existing project utilities.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI coding assistants make small, reviewable, and testable software changes.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance text and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it handle unclear requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It tells the assistant to ask one to three clarifying questions when requirements are ambiguous.

faq.question: Does it add new dependencies?
faq.answer: It guides the assistant to prefer existing repository patterns and utilities before adding dependencies.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. Its focus on small diffs and validation steps supports practical review workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe for community marketplace use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file contains no scripts, network calls, credential access, or prompt injection attempts.
